extracted.intended_audience: Readers/contributors to The American Mathematical Monthly preparing problem or solution submissions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and submitting original problems, solutions, and Classic problems to The American Mathematical Monthly via the AMM/Submittable submission manager, including required files, registration, and deadlines for solution submissions to numbered problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / not under consideration elsewhere
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted problems should not be under consideration for publication elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributors must ensure that problem proposals are original to the Monthly (unless submitted as Classics, see Classic Problem guidelines). Do not submit the same problem to other journals simultaneously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem submissions must be accompanied by solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Problem proposals must be accompanied by solutions and any bibliographical information that will assist in their review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every problem submission should include a complete solution at the time of submission; partial submissions without solutions are not acceptable for problem proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include bibliographical information
rubrics_metrics.description: Include any bibliographical information that will assist in review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide references, prior appearances, attribution, or literature pointers that help editors assess originality and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style appropriate for publication in the Monthly
rubrics_metrics.description: All contributions should be written in a style appropriate for publication in the Monthly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write clearly and in the journal's expected mathematical exposition style (suitable notation, explanation, and presentation). Ensure readability and polish consistent with the Monthly's standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred electronic file formats
rubrics_metrics.description: We encourage electronic submissions of both problems and solutions as PDF files, accompanied, when applicable, by TeX/LaTeX source files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit a PDF primary file and upload TeX/LaTeX source as secondary files when relevant to facilitate editing and typesetting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the appropriate submission form and upload files
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the appropriate form on the Submittable site to send problems or solutions; follow the web form instructions to upload Primary File and applicable Secondary Files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the correct category (Problem Proposal, Solution to Problem x, Classic Problem), fill out the form fields, attach files, and click Submit to receive an email confirmation. Use the 'Message to the editor' optional field for notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration and sign-in procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: First-time Submittable users must register by clicking the category that describes the submission; returning users should use the sign-in link.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register through the form on first use to create an account; thereafter log in via the provided link to access submission options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classic Problem criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Classics are problems of unusual elegance that are not new but deserve to be better known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting a Classic, include the problem statement, solution, and references with the submission. The Monthly will not be soliciting or publishing reader solutions to Classic problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solution-to-numbered-problem submissions: deadlines and contact
rubrics_metrics.description: Solutions to specific numbered problems have stated due dates (e.g., 'The solution is due by May 31, 2026' or later dates listed for various problems).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit solutions by the listed deadline for each problem number; if you have questions about a specific solution submission, email monthlyproblems@maa.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem Proposal category reiterated requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Problem submissions (Problem Proposal category) should be accompanied by solutions and bibliographical information; problems must not be under consideration elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reiterates the core submission requirements for the Problem Proposal category — include solution, references, and ensure exclusivity of submission.
